artworks.title: The Farnese Atlas
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Hellenistic original
artworks.description: A Roman marble statue of the Titan kneeling under the weight of the heavens, copied from a Hellenistic original. The globe on his shoulders is carved with figures of the classical constellations, making it the oldest surviving representation of the ancient celestial sphere. It is held in the National Archaeological Museum, Naples.

artworks.title: Atlas
artworks.description: An Art Deco bronze statue of Atlas straining beneath an open armillary sphere of the heavens, installed in 1937 at Rockefeller Center in New York, facing Fifth Avenue. It has become one of the most recognizable modern images of the Titan's eternal burden.

artworks.title: Atlas Holding Up the Celestial Globe
artworks.description: Guercino's Baroque Atlas strains beneath a starry globe — the Titan's eternal punishment painted as heroic musculature and night sky.

artworks.title: Atlas and the Hesperides
artworks.description: Sargent's museum mural sets Atlas under the heavens while the Hesperides rest below — the Titan's burden as a modern classical ceiling vision.

popCulture.title: Atlas Shrugged
popCulture.creator: Ayn Rand
popCulture.description: Rand's title asks who holds the world up when the Atlases of industry refuse — the Titan's burden turned into a political metaphor.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's demigod series puts Atlas back under the sky on Mount Othrys — the Titan as a boss whose burden Percy must briefly take.

popCulture.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
popCulture.creator: Santa Monica Studio
popCulture.description: Kratos chains the four-armed Titan to the Pillar of the World — Atlas forced again to bear the sky after Persephone's plot fails.

popCulture.title: Atlas (book of maps)
popCulture.creator: Gerardus Mercator
popCulture.description: Mercator named the first modern map-book Atlas after the Titan-king of Mauretania — so every book of maps still carries the heaven-bearer's name.

popCulture.title: Atlas Mountains
popCulture.description: Northwest Africa's great range took the Titan's name — Perseus' petrified Atlas rewritten as the mountains that hold up the western sky.
